chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Sulayman ibn Dawud Al-Munqari has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Isfahani, from Sulayman ibn Dawud Al-Munqari, who is known as Ibn Al-Shadhkuni.

key_terms.ابْنُ الشَّاذْكُونِيِّ: Ibn Al-Shadhkuni, an alternative name or kunya for the narrator
key_terms.الْمُنْقَرِيُّ: Al-Munqari, a nisba indicating lineage or tribe
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for the father
key_terms.سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ: Sulayman ibn Dawud, ayma n ibn Dawud, a specific narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator chain for Sulayman ibn Dawud Al-Munqari in this hadith?
ai.summary: This passage highlights Shaykh al-Saduq’s meticulous approach to verifying the isnad of Sulayman ibn Dawud Al-Munqari, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature, by tracing the transmission through his father and other reliable authorities. It underscores the scholarly emphasis on cross-referencing chains to ensure authenticity, particularly for narrators with multiple names or kunyas like Ibn Al-Shadhkuni. This biographical clarification reinforces the trustworthiness of the transmitted narrations within the Shia tradition.
